messages.subject: RTMB ADREPORT( [string_vector] )
parts:
Hi all,

RTMB offers many interesting opportunities in terms of user-interface for package authors.  One opportunity I see is that the package-user could specify a character-string and then get that set of objects available during ADREPORT (e.g., for standard errors or to apply epsilon bias-correction).

I have a little mock-up below based on the `?RTMB::MakeADFun` example ... does anyone know how to do something like this?

```R
library(RTMB)
data(rivers)

# User chooses derived quantities via string-vector outside the function declaration
derived_quantities = c("logsd")

# Function is made and not changed (e.g. by package author)
f <- function(p) {
  logsd = log(p$sd)
  out = list("logsd"=logsd)
  ADREPORT( out[derived_quantities] )
  -sum(dnorm(rivers, p$mu, p$sd, log=TRUE))
}

# GOAL:  Model is run and derived quantities available in sdreport
obj <- MakeADFun(f, list(mu=0, sd=1), silent=TRUE)
opt <- nlminb(obj$par, obj$fn, obj$gr)
sdrep = sdreport(obj)
```

messages.author: 258b98968d0ad8b9
messages.subject: Re: RTMB ADREPORT( [string_vector] )
parts:
If you use

ADREPORT( do.call("c", out[derived_quantities]) )

it 'works', i.e.. it gives the right quantities, but the names of the reported vector are lost (I think this has to be fixed in RTMB).
ADREPORT was originally made to match TMB's version, so when you do ADREPORT(x) the name literally becomes 'x'...

parts:
Thanks Kasper!

In case others are interested, it appears to be even more user-friendly if you do (as shown in full below):

```R
  derived_values = mget( derived_quantities, ifnotfound=NA)
  ADREPORT( do.call("c", derived_values) )
```

Very cool!

```R

library(RTMB)
data(rivers)

# User chooses derived quantities via string-vector outside the function declaration

# Function is made and not changed (e.g. by package author)
f <- function(p) {
  logsd = log(p$sd)

logmean = log(p$mu)
  derived_values = mget( derived_quantities, ifnotfound=NA)
  ADREPORT( do.call("c", derived_values) )

-sum(dnorm(rivers, p$mu, p$sd, log=TRUE))
}

# GOAL:  Model is run and derived quantities available in sdreport
obj <- MakeADFun(f, list(mu=0, sd=1), silent=TRUE)
opt <- nlminb(obj$par, obj$fn, obj$gr)
sdrep = sdreport(obj)
